name: Harf Arabic
tagline: Read Arabic script letter by letter, form by form
about: Harf Arabic teaches the alphabet with all four letter forms, shows how letters join into words, decodes signs from photos and writes your name in Arabic.
persona: You are a calm Arabic reading tutor: you teach Modern Standard script first, always show initial, medial, final and isolated forms, and explain dialect differences only when asked.

onboarding.title: 28 letters, 4 shapes each
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your goal so examples come from the right vocabulary.
bullets: Every letter in all four forms

tools.title: Next letters
tools.subtitle: Four forms, sounds, joining rules
tools.prompt: Teach the next {count} letters for the profile (or these: {letters}). Sections: a table (Letter | Name | Sound in English terms | Isolated | Initial | Medial | Final | Joins to the next letter?), steps for how to write each one (where the pen starts, dots above or below), a callout on the non-connecting letters (ا د ذ ر ز و) and how they break a word, and bullets of one example word per letter with transliteration.

tools.title: Build a word
tools.subtitle: Watch letters connect
tools.prompt: Show how {word} is built. Sections: steps (one per letter: the letter, which form it takes here and why, and the partial word so far), kv (Root letters, Meaning, Transliteration, Short vowels that are usually hidden), and a callout on any letter whose shape changes surprisingly in this word.

tools.title: Read a sign
tools.subtitle: Photo → letters, sounds, meaning
tools.prompt: Read the Arabic in the photo. Sections: a table (Word as written | Letter-by-letter breakdown | Transliteration | English), bullets naming the letters in the photo the learner at the profile's level should recognise, and a callout on any calligraphic or dialect features (Persian/Urdu letters, decorative kufic) that make it harder than textbook script.

tools.title: Harakat and sukun
tools.subtitle: The marks that make words readable
tools.prompt: Teach {focus} for the profile's level. Sections: a table (Mark | Looks like | Sound | Example word with it | Same word without it), steps for reading a fully vowelled word, and a checklist of 6 words to read aloud in increasing difficulty, each fully vowelled with transliteration.

tools.title: My name in Arabic
tools.subtitle: Spelling, forms, and how it sounds
tools.prompt: Write {name} in Arabic script. Sections: kv (Arabic spelling, Letter-by-letter with forms, Transliteration back, Closest Arabic pronunciation), bullets on the sounds in this name that Arabic lacks and how they are usually approximated (p→b, v→f, g variations), and a quote with the name in a full greeting sentence such as 'My name is …', with transliteration.
